audit_exclusions.query_title: Allow extensions to contribute and read resolvable variables from the workbench, Take #42
audit_exclusions.query_body: This feature has been requested by the community over and over again for the past at least 7+ years. We are going to keep asking until we get somewhere, because it seems to keep getting ignored by the team. Allow a mechanism for extensions to contribute and read resolvable variables to the workbench. This would imply extension X can contribute variables to the workbench that can be used anywhere normal variables can be used such as within tasks.json, settings.json, etc.. Additionally, the mechanism would also allow extensions to resolve variables into values. It goes both ways. I would be willing to contribute the solution to this issue myself as I have downloaded the vscode repository and have been building a proof of concept to know if this is feasible. However, I am a C, C# developer by trade and have next to no experience in the vscode architecture nor typescript. Therefore, it would be requested that someone in the know actually implement the proper interfaces. Here are screenshots from my proof of concept I don't know what will be accepted for the 'mechanism' by which to do this. However this is one such concrete proposal. 1. Add a new variable form to the existing forms such as command, input etc. The form would be ${var:extension.variable}. 2. Extensions can contribute / register a single callback to the workbench that gets executed when the variable form is encountered. The resolver holds a map of extension ids to callbacks 3. The resolver logic traps on the 'var' in the switch statement above and parses the extension id. The resolver looks in the extension map. If the extension exists within the map, it executes the callback 4. Within the extension callback, the extension uses its own logic for tracking contributed variables and returns a string back to the resolver of the variable value. The variable value itself can contain embedded resolvable variables. 5. Extensions can also call a now publicized method on the resolver to resolve a variable and get the value of the variable The other option would be for the resolver to hold a map that extensions can contribute to directly. However, I think this may cause conflict between extensions if multiple extensions try to contribute or use the same name of a variable. In the above example, I have a variable in a task called 'thebaz'. To use it within tasks.json the form is ${var:myextension.thebaz}. The variable contains an embedded variable called thefoob. The resolver resolves this to ${var:myextension.thefoob}. The resolver then resolves ${var:myextension.thefoob} to 'FOOBED!' The proof of concept proves this is very doable as the plumbing for the recursive resolution is already in place. Current trigger for this request is : #46471

audit_exclusions.query_body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.122.1 (user setup)
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Open or create a new untitled Markdown file. Fill it with enough lines (e.g. 200 lines of `1\n\n` each) so the preview height exceeds the screen.
2. Scroll the editor to the top, then use `Ctrl+Shift+V` (`markdown.togglePreview`) to enter preview.
3. Scroll the preview to the bottom, then use `Ctrl+Shift+V` again to exit preview. Observe that the editor now shows the last few lines at the top — the scroll position has been "locked" to the source line corresponding to the top of the preview at exit.
4. Scroll the editor back to the top (via scroll wheel or `Ctrl+Home`).
5. Switch to another editor (any language), then switch back to the Markdown editor — using mouse click, `Ctrl+Tab` (`workbench.action.nextEditor` / `workbench.action.previousEditor`), or `Alt+←` (`workbench.action.navigateBack`).
6. **Bug**: The editor jumps back to the locked position from step 3. When switching back from another editor group via mouse click, the click-down event triggers an immediate scroll, which also creates an unintended text selection (as if the user were holding the mouse button while scrolling).

**Notes**:

- The issue persists with `--disable-extensions` (but built-in Markdown extension is still active).
- The following settings do NOT fix it:
- `"markdown.preview.scrollPreviewWithEditor": false`
- `"markdown.preview.scrollEditorWithPreview": false`
- `code --user-data-dir "$env:TEMP\vscode-clean-test" --disable-extensions` to create a window with clean profile
- The "locked" position is essentially the source line that was at the top of the preview when `togglePreview` was last used to exit preview mode. The editor remains bound to that scroll position until the next reload, even after manually scrolling away.

audit_exclusions.query_title: Add visibility/hidden flag to LanguageModelChatInformation to control Model Picker disclosure
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### Problem
When language model providers expose new models via `provideLanguageModelChatInformation()`, all new models are automatically **visible by default** in the Model Picker. This forces users to manually visit the Language Models configuration screen to hide models they don't want to see every time new models are added by a provider.

### Use Case
Language model providers (like MiniMax, Anthropic, Google, etc.) regularly release new models. Users should have the option to:
1. Have new models appear as **hidden by default** in the Model Picker
2. Manually unhide only the models they want to use
3. Without having to manage visibility each time a new model is released

### Proposed Solution
Add an optional `hidden?: boolean` property to the `LanguageModelChatInformation` interface:

```typescript
export interface LanguageModelChatInformation {
readonly id: string
readonly name: string
readonly family: string
readonly tooltip?: string
readonly detail?: string
readonly version: string
readonly maxInputTokens: number
readonly maxOutputTokens: number
readonly capabilities: LanguageModelChatCapabilities
readonly hidden?: boolean // NEW: Optional flag to hide from Model Picker by default
}
```

### Expected Behavior
- If `hidden: true` → model is registered but hidden from the Model Picker dropdown; it remains accessible in the Language Models configuration screen for users to unhide if needed
- If `hidden: false` or omitted → model appears in both Language Models list and Model Picker (current behavior)
- Users can still toggle visibility manually in the Language Models configuration screen

### Impact
- ✅ Better UX for power users who want curated model lists
- ✅ Providers can expose experimental/niche models without cluttering the picker
- ✅ Backward compatible (existing providers continue to work with default visible behavior)
audit_exclusions.target_title: vscode.lm — Add model visibility (hide/show) APIs

audit_exclusions.query_title: Restrict skills to specific agents
audit_exclusions.query_body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem
At the moment, there is no feature to restrict specific skills to a particular agent, which can lead to unnecessary skill exposure and less controlled behavior. Clear skill-to-agent assignment would help improve accuracy, reduce misuse, and keep agent responsibilities more focused.

## Proposed solution
Add a way to bind or restrict skills to selected agents only. For example, a skill could be marked as available only for one agent, or for a defined list of agents, instead of being globally accessible.

## Why this is useful
- Improves separation of responsibilities between agents.
- Prevents irrelevant skills from being used by the wrong agent.
- Makes agent behaviour more predictable and easier to manage.
- Could also help reduce unnecessary token usage by limiting skill selection.

## Suggested implementation
Possible approaches:
- Add an `allowed_agents` field in skill definitions.

## Additional context
This would be especially useful in multi-agent systems where each agent has a dedicated role and should only use the tools or skills relevant to that role.

Type: Bug I’m reporting a serious reliability failure in Copilot Chat that caused loss of active working context and wasted paid usage. A large set of in-progress Copilot Chat conversations that had been visible daily for weeks disappeared from the sidebar with no warning, no migration notice, and no practical recovery flow in the product. This was not cosmetic inconvenience. It was loss of working state tied to active tasks, decisions, and technical context accumulated over time. Impact: Significant loss of work context across multiple ongoing efforts. Additional paid premium requests consumed to reconstruct missing context. Direct productivity loss and trust erosion in Copilot Chat as a paid tool. What makes this unacceptable is not only the disappearance itself, but the mismatch between product behavior and user expectation. The UI presents chat history as persistent working memory, but update/reset behavior appears to treat it like fragile local cache. If history is non-durable, users must be clearly warned. If history is intended to persist, this is a data durability defect. Expected behavior: Durable, version-safe chat history retention. Explicit migration and recovery path during extension/app updates. Built-in export and backup controls for user-owned conversation history. Clear warning before any operation that could orphan or clear chat indexes/state. This issue should be treated as a high-severity reliability problem for paid customers. The current behavior causes real lost work and real financial cost. audit_exclusions.query_title: Copilot Plan/Agent back button creates a new chat session and automatically sends Start implementation
audit_exclusions.query_body:
## Description

When using the Copilot Plan / Agent workflow, after an implementation task has completed, clicking the back/return button can unexpectedly create a new chat window/session and automatically send the message:

```text
Start implementation
```

This appears to replay or restart the previous implementation action even though the prior task has already finished.

This is similar to #323996, but in this case the behavior also creates/opens a new chat window or session before sending `Start implementation` automatically.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Copilot Chat in VS Code Insiders.
2. Use the Plan / Agent workflow to create and start an implementation task.
3. Wait until the implementation task completes.
4. Click the back/return button to go back to the previous Plan/Chat state.

## Expected Behavior

Clicking back/return after the task is completed should only restore the previous Plan/Chat view.

It should not create a new chat window/session, and it should not automatically send `Start implementation` again.

## Actual Behavior

VS Code creates/opens a new chat window/session and automatically sends:

```text
Start implementation
```

without user confirmation.

## Impact

This can accidentally start another implementation run, consume additional Copilot quota/credits, and make it difficult to safely return to the previous planning session after a completed task.

## Environment

- VS Code Version: Code - Insiders 1.128.0-insider
- Commit: 3fbc14e67322245a87adf07c3da0c487e7715918
- Architecture: x64
- OS: Windows
- Workflow: Copilot Plan / Agent
- Trigger: after implementation completes, click back/return

## Notes

I searched for related reports before filing this. #323996 appears related, but the additional behavior here is that a new chat window/session is created before `Start implementation` is sent automatically.

audit_exclusions.query_title: Copilot Chat renders `./...` inside inline code as a parent-folder inline reference
audit_exclusions.query_body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: built-in VS Code `copilot` extension from `C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\fcf604774b\resources\app\extensions\copilot`; `code --list-extensions --show-versions` does not list `GitHub.copilot-chat`
- VS Code Version: 1.125.1 (`fcf604774b9f2674b473065736ee75077e256353`, x64)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 25H2, OS build 26200.8246, Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.297.0
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Chat panel, Ask mode / normal chat response rendering
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Custom API via UnifyChatProvider, GPT-5.5
- Logs: I have an exported `chat.json`; relevant excerpt is included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code with a workspace nested inside a named parent folder, for example:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\repro-parent\repro-workspace
```

2. Open Copilot Chat.

3. Ask Copilot Chat to repeat a command containing `./...` inside inline code:

```text
Please repeat this exact command in inline code: `go test ./...`
```

4. If it does not reproduce on the first try, add workspace/file context and ask again:

```text
The correct command is `go test ./...`. Repeat only the command in inline code.
```

Expected:

The chat response should visibly render exactly:

```text
go test ./...
```

Actual:

The stored model/tool-round response is correct, but the rendered chat message can replace `./..` with an inline file/folder reference to the parent directory and leave the final `.` as text.

In my case the workspace was under:

```text
C:\Users\gyli\Desktop\Misc-local\pylink\jlink-cli
```

The parent folder was `pylink`, so the UI rendered the command as:

```text
go test pylink.
```

Evidence from the exported chat JSON:

The stored final response for request 8 is correct:

```json
"response": "μ¡úτí«σåàσ«╣μÿ»∩╝Ü\n\n`go test ./...`"
```

But the rendered response parts were split into text + inlineReference + text:

```json
[
{ "value": "μ¡úτí«σåàσ«╣μÿ»∩╝Ü\n\n`go test " },
{
"kind": "inlineReference",
"inlineReference": {
"fsPath": "c:\\Users\\gyli\\Desktop\\Misc-local\\pylink",
"path": "/C:/Users/gyli/Desktop/Misc-local/pylink",
"scheme": "file"
}
},
{ "value": ".`" }
]
```

This appears to turn `./...` into:

```text
./.. -> inlineReference to parent folder "pylink"
. -> remaining literal dot
```

Impact:

- The visible chat output changes the literal content of a command inside inline code.
- It makes users think the model generated the wrong command even when the stored response is correct.
- `go test ./...` is a common Go command, so this is easy to hit in development chats.
- The same issue may affect other command tokens containing `./...` or similar relative path syntax.

Possible implementation clue:

This looks related to chat inline reference annotation/linkification rather than model output. It may be near chat inline reference handling in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/widget/annotations.ts` or `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatMarkdownContentPart.ts`. There appears to already be coverage for inline references inside backtick code spans, but `./...` may be a missing edge case where `./..` is recognized as a path reference before/while code-span handling runs.

audit_exclusions.query_title: editorContext reports last focused file instead of empty when no editor is open (Copilot Chat)
audit_exclusions.query_body:
## Summary

When no file is open in the editor (e.g. the Source Control view is active and no editor tabs are present), Copilot Chat still reports the **last focused file** as the current file via `editorContext`. It should report no file / empty context.

## Environment

- **VS Code version:** Insiders
- **Extension:** GitHub Copilot Chat

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a file in the editor (e.g. `SomeProject.csproj`)
2. Switch focus to the **Source Control** view (or any other view with no editor tab active)
3. Close or navigate away so there is no active editor tab
4. Ask Copilot Chat: *"What file do I have open?"* or *"What is my current branch?"*

## Expected Behavior

`editorContext` should be empty / null, and Copilot Chat should respond that no file is currently open.

## Actual Behavior

Copilot Chat reports the last file that was open before focus moved away:

> *"The user's current file is `c:\...\SomeProject.csproj`"*

The title bar shows **"Untitled (Workspace)"** confirming no editor is active, yet the stale file path is still injected into the prompt context.

## Impact

Copilot uses the stale `editorContext` to make incorrect inferences — for example, guessing which workspace repo is "active" based on a file that is no longer open. This can lead to misleading answers about the current working context.

## Screenshot

The VS Code window shows Source Control view active, title bar reads "Untitled (Workspace)", no editor tabs open — yet Copilot continues to report the previously open `.csproj` file as the current file.

## Additional Notes

This was observed in a multi-root workspace with two repositories open. The stale file path belonged to `delaget-polling-loading`, which caused Copilot to select that repo as "current" over `delaget-dbup` when neither was definitively active.
audit_exclusions.target_title: Copilot Chat Agent uses wrong session/file context when multiple chat sessions are active

audit_exclusions.query_body:

<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.129.1
- OS Version: Latest version

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Using the Tree View API create the following structure:

```
[ ] One
----[ ] Two
----Three
--------Four
```

Notice the following:
- One level of indent has 4 dashes
- Lines with `[ ]` have the `ThreeItem.checkboxState` property set to `Checked` or `Unchecked`

2. Then add the Five node without a checkbox as a sibling to Three:

```
[ ] One
----[ ] Two
----Three
--------Four
----Five
```

The previous graph shows how it should look but instead it looks like this:

```
[ ] One
-[ ] Two
----Three
--------Four
----Five
```

As we can see, for some reason the nodes with a checkbox get an incorrect indent.

**Note**: I have to mention that I detected this issue while using my extension [Task Tree](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=andres-munoz.tasktree) but since there is not option in the Tree View API to control the visual indent of the nodes I believe that it is an issue in the Tree View API.

This is further to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316867 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321136. To avoid supply chain attacks, support was added for an "auto update delay" for auto-updated extensions.

But as noted in those issues, there is also a scenario in which updates are performed manually. Many of us don't blindly auto-update.

In such a case, 1) embargoed updates should be hidden until the delay is reached, or 2) if they are shown then the UI should caution the user that they are still embargoed.

I've added this dedicated feature request so it isn't forgotten.

Thank you!

## Summary

VS Code 1.129 experiences **intermittent renderer process crashes** (exit code 135) on Ubuntu 24.04 with NVIDIA GPU. The crashes started immediately after updating to 1.129 today. Crashpad has captured **11 dump files** throughout the day.

A recurring JavaScript error appears in `renderer.log` prior to crashes:
```
Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left')
at w_t.prepareRender (workbench.desktop.main.js:519:79187)
```

## Environment

- **VS Code Version:** 1.129.0, commit `125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7`, x64
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.02 LTS
- **Kernel:** 6.17.0-40-generic
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Max-Q / Mobile
- **GPU Driver:** 595.71.05
- **Display Server:** X11
- **Install Method:** Official `.deb` package from `packages.microsoft.com/repos/code`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Update VS Code to 1.129 via apt
2. Launch VS Code (from terminal or desktop — both paths exhibit the same behavior)
3. Use VS Code normally (open files, edit, switch tabs)
4. **Intermittently**, the window crashes with "窗口意外终止(原因: \"crashed\", 代码: \"135\")"
5. Crashpad generates a `.dmp` file in `~/.config/Code/Crashpad/completed/`

## Observed Crash Timeline (today)

| Time | Dump File | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| 10:49 | `a53276d0-...` | First crash after update |
| 11:11 | `73ea0dc1-...` | |
| 13:30 | `a38773d3-...` | |
| 13:30 | `ab44e9af-...` | |

| 13:39 | `31142c13-...` | |
| 13:39 | `7b351fea-...` | |
| 13:39 | `961036aa-...` | |
| 13:56 | `f39ba203-...` | |
| 14:32 | `26ef0781-...` | Most recent crash |

## Key Logs

### renderer.log — Recurring JS error (appears 8+ times before crashes)

```
[error] Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left'): TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left')
at w_t.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:519:79187)
at JTt.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:519:31984)
at Object.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:22798)
at Object.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:21259)
at vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:27042
at vZ (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:25970)
at s._onRenderScheduled (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:27033)
at h9e.e [as _runner] (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:26591)
at h9e.execute (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:439:3974)
at i (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:439:4219)
```

This error occurs in the **view rendering pipeline** (`prepareRender`), suggesting a DOM/view model element is unexpectedly `null` when `.left` is accessed.

### main.log — No obvious crash signature

```
2026-07-16 14:10:43.192 [info] StorageMainService: creating application shared storage
2026-07-16 14:10:43.260 [info] update#setState idle
2026-07-16 14:11:13.260 [info] update#setState checking for updates
2026-07-16 14:11:13.489 [info] update#setState idle

```
[ERROR:third_party/crashpad/crashpad/util/file/file_io_posix.cc:153]
open /home/changli/.config/Code/Crashpad/pending/983b8568-1d6f-43d5-94b5-a3e42bc390b4.lock: File exists (17)
```

A stale lock file persists, suggesting a previous crash dump write was interrupted.

## Other Errors in renderer.log

- `MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 error listeners added to [WriteStream]`
- `MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 drain listeners added to [WriteStream]`
- Extension API proposal errors: `Tencent-Cloud.coding-copilot CANNOT USE these API proposals`
- `vscode.mermaid-markdown-features CANNOT use 'legacyToolReferenceFullNames'`

## Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?

**Testing in progress.** Fresh launch with `--disable-extensions` succeeds, but since the crash is intermittent, longer observation is needed.

## What was ruled out

- **Launch method difference**: Both terminal (`code`) and desktop entry (`/usr/share/code/code`) exhibit identical single-instance behavior. The crash is not related to how VS Code is launched.
- **Immediate startup crash**: VS Code starts successfully. Crashes occur during normal use.

## Possibly related issues

- #312100 — Copilot chat crashes VS Code every 2 minutes with code 135 (Linux, 1.114-1.117)
- #209921 — VS Code crashes on startup with error code 135 (Fedora, 1.86-1.88)
- #314075 — Extension host crashes with code 133 on 1.118.1

## Suggested next steps for triage

1. Symbolicate the crash dumps to identify the exact renderer crash site
2. Investigate the `prepareRender` null pointer error at `workbench.desktop.main.js:519:79187`
3. Check if the `MaxListenersExceededWarning` EventEmitter leak is related to the crash
4. Verify whether disabling extensions prevents the crash over extended use

audit_exclusions.query_title: Extension host crashes deterministically with SIGTRAP (code 133, INT3 at fixed binary offset 0x431ea0d) on 1.118.1 — downgrade to 1.117.0 fixes it
audit_exclusions.query_body:
## Summary

Extension host process aborts with `SIGTRAP` (`code: 133`) approximately every 30–90 seconds after activation on **VS Code 1.118.1** (Linux x64). The crash is **deterministic**: every kernel `trap int3` lands on the **same offset within the `code` binary** (`0x431ea0d`), independent of which extensions are loaded — including with most third-party extensions disabled, leaving only bundled `vscode.*` + `GitHub.copilot-chat`.

**Downgrading to 1.117.0** (latest available patch of the 1.117 branch) **fully resolves the crash** with the same configuration, same workspace, same enabled extensions. After the downgrade: 0 crashes, 0 INT3 traps in `dmesg`, no Bisect prompts.

## Environment

- **VS Code (broken)**: `1.118.1`, commit `034f571df509819cc10b0c8129f66ef77a542f0e`, x64
- **VS Code (working)**: `1.117.0`, commit `10c8e557c8b9f9ed0a87f61f1c9a44bde731c409`, x64
- **OS**: Ubuntu, Linux 5.4.0-228-generic, x86_64
- **Install method**: apt (`packages.microsoft.com/repos/code stable`)
- **NODE_OPTIONS**: `--max-old-space-size=8192` (does not prevent the crash)
- **System RAM**: 64 GiB, 0 swap, ~22 GiB free at crash time (no system OOM)

## Reproduction

1. Install VS Code 1.118.1 from the official Microsoft apt repo.
2. Open a multi-folder workspace (~6 large repos / hundreds of thousands of files).
3. Wait 30–90 s after the extension host starts.
4. The extension host dies with `code: 133`.
5. VS Code restarts the host automatically; the cycle repeats indefinitely (~13 crashes in ~50 minutes observed).
6. After several cycles, VS Code shows the "Extension Bisect" suggestion dialog every few launches.

## Evidence

### `~/.config/Code/logs/<session>/main.log` — repeated identical signature

```
2026-05-04 12:17:52.417 [info] Extension host with pid 452795 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:17:52.418 [error] [UtilityProcess id: 1, type: extensionHost, pid: 452795]: crashed with code 133 and reason 'crashed'
2026-05-04 12:18:55.210 [info] Extension host with pid 465698 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:19:51.628 [info] Extension host with pid 476370 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:22:36.790 [info] Extension host with pid 487965 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:23:19.063 [info] Extension host with pid 493193 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:24:37.633 [info] Extension host with pid 500647 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:25:36.791 [info] Extension host with pid 510472 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
2026-05-04 12:26:35.104 [info] Extension host with pid 520152 exited with code: 133, signal: unknown.
```

### `dmesg` (kernel) — `INT3` at fixed binary offset (smoking gun)

```
[12:17:57] traps: code[452795] trap int3 ip:55927c8d6a0d in code[5592785b8000+8d4e000]
[12:19:00] traps: code[465698] trap int3 ip:56148970ca0d in code[5614853ee000+8d4e000]
[12:19:57] traps: code[476378] trap int3 ip:55a3c8f11a0d in code[55a3c4bf3000+8d4e000]
[12:24:43] traps: code[500647] trap int3 ip:555daafc0a0d in code[555da6ca2000+8d4e000]
[12:25:42] traps: code[510472] trap int3 ip:55bb8c8e9a0d in code[55bb885cb000+8d4e000]
[12:26:40] traps: code[520152] trap int3 ip:56171f5a7a0d in code[56171b289000+8d4e000]
```

Computing `ip - base` for each crash:

| crash | ip | base | ip − base |
|---|---|---|---|
| 452795 | `0x55927c8d6a0d` | `0x5592785b8000` | `0x431ea0d` |
| 465698 | `0x56148970ca0d` | `0x5614853ee000` | `0x431ea0d` |
| 476378 | `0x55a3c8f11a0d` | `0x55a3c4bf3000` | `0x431ea0d` |
| 500647 | `0x555daafc0a0d` | `0x555da6ca2000` | `0x431ea0d` |
| 510472 | `0x55bb8c8e9a0d` | `0x55bb885cb000` | `0x431ea0d` |
| 520152 | `0x56171f5a7a0d` | `0x56171b289000` | `0x431ea0d` |

**Same instruction in the binary on every crash, despite ASLR.** This is a deterministic V8/Node `CHECK()` failure (`INT3` instruction = SIGTRAP = exit code 133) inside the extensionHost process.

### `renderer.log` — last crash with most third-party extensions disabled

```
2026-05-04 12:22:36.792 [error] Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 487965) terminated unexpectedly. The following extensions were running: vscode.github-authentication, vscode.emmet, GitHub.copilot-chat, vscode.git-base, vscode.microsoft-authentication, vscode.git, vscode.github, vscode.npm, vscode.terminal-suggest, vscode.configuration-editing, vscode.json-language-features, vscode.typescript-language-features, vscode.debug-auto-launch, vscode.merge-conflict, vscode.extension-editing
```

All `vscode.*` are bundled. Only non-bundled extension still active: `GitHub.copilot-chat` (preinstalled with VS Code 1.118+). **The crash still happened.**

### Crashpad

**No `.dmp` files written for these INT3 crashes** in `~/.config/Code/Crashpad/completed/` during the affected sessions (last dump was 2026-04-27). Crashpad is not catching this signal in 1.118.1 — possibly a separate issue, but reduces diagnostic value.

## Workaround that fully resolves the issue

```bash
apt download code=1.117.0-1776814346 # available in same MS apt repo
sudo dpkg -i code_1.117.0-1776814346_amd64.deb
sudo apt-mark hold code
```

After this, with the same workspace and same enabled extensions:
- 0 crashes `code: 133` in `main.log`
- 0 `trap int3` in `dmesg`
- No Bisect prompts
- Extension host stable across reloads

## What was ruled out

- **Specific third-party extensions**: crashes persisted after disabling/uninstalling several extensions,tried with only bundled `vscode.*` + `GitHub.copilot-chat` remained, still crashed.
- **System OOM**: `dmesg` shows no `oom_kill`, system has 22+ GiB free.
- **V8 heap limit**: setting `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` does not prevent the crash.
- **Kilo Code orphan child processes** (a real but separate bug — Kilo's `kilo serve` sidecar leaks on each ext host crash; killing 24 leaked sidecars freed 6.7 GiB but did not stop the crash loop).
- **Crashpad capturing it**: no minidump produced for these specific INT3 traps.

## Possibly related issues (different exit codes / different versions, not exact duplicates)

- #312100 — Copilot chat crashes VS Code every 2 minutes with `code 135` error (Linux, 1.114-1.117)
- #311225 — Copilot Chat: Memory leaks and crashed
- #307897 — Extension host crashes with `promptCacheKey` TypeError → exit 134 (SIGABRT)
- #311316 — It crashes after each 5 minutes (Linux x64)

This appears to be a **1.118.1-specific regression** of the same family of extensionHost lifecycle bugs — distinct because of the deterministic `INT3` at the same binary offset, and because **downgrade to 1.117.0 fully fixes it for this configuration**, while #312100 reports 1.117 still affected with a different exit code.

## Suggested next steps for triage

- Symbolicate offset `0x431ea0d` in the 1.118.1 `code` binary (commit `034f571df509819cc10b0c8129f66ef77a542f0e`) to identify the V8 `CHECK()` site.
- Check whether Crashpad signal-handling configuration changed between 1.117.0 → 1.118.1 (separate but useful — would have given proper minidumps).

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
I’d like to request a feature that exposes the number of credits used in GitHub Copilot Chat sessions within Visual Studio Code.

As a GitHub Copilot Enterprise user, I currently don’t have a clear way to understand how many credits I’ve used while working in chat. The only option I currently have is to check the number of credits consumed at the end of a chat. There seems to be no way to access this data programmatically (for example through an API surface). This makes it difficult to track usage, understand consumption patterns, and manage usage expectations over time.

### Requested behavior
Please add a way to access programmatically credit usage in Visual Studio Code for Copilot Chat. For example, APIs could expose:

- Credits used for the current chat session
- Credits used per prompt or response
- A running total for the current day, week, or month.

### Why this would help
For Enterprise users especially, usage transparency is important because:

- we may not have direct visibility into consumption during normal development workflows
- it helps us better understand how our Copilot usage maps to our plan
- it would improve trust and predictability when using chat heavily
- it would help teams and users make more informed decisions about usage

### Suggested outcome
Even a simple usage indicator or link to live credit consumption from within VS Code would be very valuable.

Many thanks in advance.

audit_exclusions.query_title: Regression: Postman extension fails to load items on VS Code 1.128.0 ("Unable to load items. Retry")
audit_exclusions.query_body:
## Summary

After updating Visual Studio Code to `1.128.0`, the Postman extension no longer loads its items correctly on Windows.

The extension shows the message:

`Unable to load items. Retry`

Clicking `Retry` has no effect, and the extension remains stuck without loading any content.

Downgrading VS Code back to `1.127.x` restores normal behavior immediately.

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install and use the Postman extension in VS Code on Windows
2. Update VS Code to version `1.128.0`
3. Open the Postman extension sidebar/view
4. Wait for the extension to load workspace items
5. Observe the error message
6. Click `Retry`

---

## Actual result

- The extension shows: `Unable to load items. Retry`
- Clicking `Retry` does nothing
- No items are loaded
- The extension remains unusable in this state

---

## Expected result

The Postman extension should load items normally and allow access to workspace content, as it did before the VS Code update.

---

## Regression

Yes, this appears to be a regression.

- Works on: `VS Code 1.127.x`
- Fails on: `VS Code 1.128.0`

The issue disappears completely after downgrading VS Code from `1.128.0` to `1.127.x`.

---

## Environment

- VS Code: `1.128.0 (user setup)`
- Commit: `fc3def6774c76082adf699d366f31a557ce5573f`
- Date: `2026-07-07T15:14:24-07:00`
- Electron: `42.5.0`
- ElectronBuildId: `14525058`
- Chromium: `148.0.7778.271`
- Node.js: `24.17.0`
- V8: `14.8.178.33-electron.0`
- OS: `Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200`

---

## Troubleshooting already attempted

I tried the following before identifying the VS Code version as the likely cause:

- Restarted extensions
- Reinstalled the Postman extension

These steps did not resolve the issue while using VS Code `1.128.0`.

---

## Workaround

Downgraded VS Code to `1.127.x`.

After downgrading, the Postman extension started working normally again without any additional changes.

---

## Impact

This issue prevents the extension from loading workspace items at all, which makes it effectively unusable on VS Code `1.128.0`.

---

## Additional notes

Based on the behavior and the successful downgrade test, this looks like a compatibility issue or regression triggered specifically by VS Code `1.128.0` on Windows.

If helpful, I can also provide:

- Postman extension logs
- VS Code Developer Tools console output
- Screenshots of the error state

audit_exclusions.query_title: Empty chat widget when opening an archived worktree agent session
audit_exclusions.query_body:
Opening a recently-archived, worktree-isolated Copilot agent session shows an **empty chat widget** with no transcript.

### Cause
Archiving a worktree-isolated session deletes its on-disk worktree (keeping the branch). On resume, the Copilot SDK requires the session's working directory to exist to bring the session up — the only path to reading the transcript. Both `resumeSession` and its `createSession` fallback pass the deleted worktree path and fail with `Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed`, so the session is restored with `0 turns` → empty model. The failure was also swallowed, so no error was shown.

### Fix (tracked by [#324341](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/324341))
- Enforce read-only for archived (and other read-only) chats via chat interactivity, so a read-only/archived session never runs a turn.
- Repair a missing working directory on resume: archived sessions resume against the repository root for history only; a live session whose worktree was deleted has its worktree recreated from the persisted branch (`git worktree add -f`, to handle the deleted-but-still-registered case).
- Surface unrecoverable load failures (e.g. the underlying git error) to the UI instead of a silently empty session.
- Show an archived-specific read-only banner with an inline **Restore** action.

### Repro
1. Create a Copilot agent session with worktree isolation and run a few turns.
2. Archive the session.
3. Reopen it from the sessions list.
4. Before the fix: empty chat widget. After the fix: transcript renders read-only with a Restore action.

audit_exclusions.query_title: Terminal isn't openning
audit_exclusions.query_body:
# Bug Report: Terminal exits immediately (code 0) on macOS arm64 — xterm.js WebGL dispose race condition

**Type:** Bug

## Description

When opening a new integrated terminal on VS Code Insiders 1.119.0 (macOS arm64),
the terminal closes immediately. Investigation via trace logs reveals two related issues:

1. The zsh process exits cleanly (code `0`) ~300ms after spawning
2. The terminal dispose triggered by the early exit causes an **uncaught TypeError**
in xterm.js's WebGL renderer during cleanup

Reproduced with **all extensions disabled** (`--disable-extensions`).

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch with `code-insiders --disable-extensions --log trace`
2. Open a new terminal via `` Ctrl+` ``
3. Observe that the terminal panel flashes and immediately closes
4. Open **Help > Toggle Developer Tools** and observe the uncaught TypeError in the console

**Expected:** Terminal opens and displays a shell prompt.
**Actual:** Terminal closes immediately; an uncaught TypeError is thrown during disposal.

---

## Console Error (Developer Tools)

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')
at get dimensions (xterm.js:1:242728)
at _._refreshCanvasDimensions (xterm.js:1:381740)
at _._refreshDecorations (xterm.js:1:382114)
at xterm.js:1:383646
```

**Call stack leading to the error:**

```
_disposeOfWebglRenderer @ xtermTerminal.ts:974
dispose @ xtermTerminal.ts:1088
dispose @ terminalInstance.ts:1300
_onProcessExit @ terminalInstance.ts:1740
_onExit @ terminalProcessManager.ts:705
handleExit @ basePty.ts:67
```

The WebGL renderer is disposed during `_onProcessExit`, but a pending
`requestAnimationFrame` callback (`_queueRefresh → _refreshDecorations`) still
runs after disposal and tries to access `dimensions` on an already-destroyed object.

---

## Pty Host Log (key events)

```
11:36:38.409 node-pty.IPty#spawn /bin/zsh ["-il"] — PID 20700 created
11:36:38.485 onProcessReady {pid: 20700} — process ready
11:36:38.488 TerminalProcess#_queueProcessExit — exit queued (~79ms after spawn)
11:36:38.744 PtyService#_onProcessExit {code: 0} — clean exit
```

The shell exits with code `0` — no crash, no signal. The zsh process terminates
almost immediately after the shell integration scripts are injected
(`VSCODE_INJECTION=1`, `ZDOTDIR` overridden to temp path for shell integration).

<details>
<summary>Full Pty Host log</summary>

```
2026-05-01 11:36:38.404 [trace] [RPC Request] PtyService#createProcess(...)
2026-05-01 11:36:38.404 [trace] [RPC Response] PtyService#createProcess 1
2026-05-01 11:36:38.404 [trace] [RPC Request] PtyService#start(1)
2026-05-01 11:36:38.409 [trace] node-pty.IPty#spawn /bin/zsh ["-il"] {...}
2026-05-01 11:36:38.485 [trace] [RPC Event] PtyService#_onProcessReady.fire({"id":1,"event":{"pid":20700,"cwd":"/Users/mfc/Developer/ozempicado"}})
2026-05-01 11:36:38.485 [trace] [RPC Response] PtyService#start {"injectedArgs":["-il"]}
2026-05-01 11:36:38.488 [trace] TerminalProcess#_queueProcessExit
at Ue._queueProcessExit (ptyHostMain.js:409:10776)
at ReadStream.<anonymous> (node-pty/lib/terminal.js:93:76)
at ReadStream.emit (node:events:519:28)
at Terminal.emit (node-pty/lib/terminal.js:155:34)
2026-05-01 11:36:38.744 [trace] node-pty.IPty#kill
2026-05-01 11:36:38.744 [trace] [RPC Event] PtyService#_onProcessExit.fire({"id":1,"event":0})
2026-05-01 11:36:39.285 [trace] [RPC Request] PtyService#setTerminalLayoutInfo({"tabs":[]})
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full Terminal (frontend) log</summary>

```
2026-05-01 11:36:17.828 [trace] [45bcad4] Reconnected to local terminals []
2026-05-01 11:36:17.828 [trace] [45bcad4] Pty host ready []
2026-05-01 11:36:38.175 [trace] [45bcad4] terminalInstance#ctor (instanceId: 1)
2026-05-01 11:36:38.258 [debug] [45bcad4] Starting pty host []
2026-05-01 11:36:38.283 [trace] [45bcad4] Webgl was loaded []
2026-05-01 11:36:38.485 [debug] [45bcad4] onProcessReady [{"pid":20700,"cwd":"/Users/mfc/Developer/ozempicado"}]
2026-05-01 11:36:38.485 [debug] [45bcad4] Terminal process ready (shellProcessId: 20700) []
2026-05-01 11:36:38.746 [debug] [45bcad4] Terminal process exit ["instanceId",1,"code",0,"processState",4]
2026-05-01 11:36:38.746 [trace] [45bcad4] terminalInstance#dispose (instanceId: 1) []
```

</details>

---

## Analysis

### Issue 1 — Shell exits immediately (possible shell integration conflict)

Shell integration overrides `ZDOTDIR` to a temp directory
(`/private/var/folders/.../mfc-code-insiders-zsh`) so the injection script runs
before the user's dotfiles. The zsh exits with code `0`, suggesting either the
injection script or an interaction with the user's `.zshrc` / `.zprofile` is
causing an early exit.

**Suggested workaround to test:**

```json
"terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled": false
```

### Issue 2 — xterm.js WebGL dispose race condition (VS Code bug)

When the terminal process exits, `_disposeOfWebglRenderer` is called synchronously,
but a `requestAnimationFrame`-deferred call to `_refreshDecorations` still holds a
reference to the renderer and accesses `dimensions` after it is already `undefined`.

This is a **use-after-dispose race condition** that should be reproducible whenever
any terminal process exits very quickly — not specific to this machine's configuration.

**Suggested workaround to test:**

```json
"terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration": "off"
```

---

## Environment

|------|-------|
| VS Code | Code - Insiders 1.119.0-insider (commit `43d0ed4`, 2026-04-30) |
| OS | macOS Darwin arm64 25.2.0 |
| Machine | MacBook Pro M4 (16.1) |
| Shell | `/bin/zsh` (system default) |
| Shell integration | Enabled (`VSCODE_INJECTION=1`) |
| Extensions disabled during repro | Yes (`--disable-extensions`) |
| GPU | Apple M4 / ANGLE Metal Renderer (WebGL enabled) |
| Memory | 24 GB (0.14 GB free at time of repro) |

audit_exclusions.query_title: Feature Request: Allow custom agents to specify a model when invoking subagents via runSubagent
audit_exclusions.query_body:
## Feature Request

### Problem

Custom agents (`.agent.md`) can specify a `model:` in their own frontmatter, and parent agents can invoke subagents via `runSubagent`. However, there is no way for a parent agent to **override the subagent's model at invocation time**. The `runSubagent` tool accepts `prompt`, `description`, and `agentName` — but no `model` parameter.

This means that if an orchestrator agent wants to run the same subagent with different models at different stages of a workflow, the only options are:

1. **Duplicate the agent file** with a different `model:` in frontmatter (e.g., `qa-investigator.agent.md` + `qa-investigator-gpt5.agent.md` with identical bodies)
2. **Ask the user to manually switch models** in the picker between stages

Neither is ideal. Option 1 creates maintenance burden (two identical agent bodies to keep in sync). Option 2 breaks automation flow and requires human intervention mid-workflow.

### Use Case: Cross-Model QA Validation

I maintain a multi-agent fix workflow with three custom agents:

- **fix-planner** — researches and plans the fix
- **fix-issue** — orchestrates the full lifecycle (plan → implement → QA → PR)
- **qa-investigator** — read-only edge-case reviewer, invoked as a subagent by fix-issue

The QA phase runs iterative review cycles until the qa-investigator finds zero issues. A significant quality improvement comes from **cross-model validation**: after the QA loop passes clean with one model (e.g., Claude Opus), re-running the same QA agent with a different model (e.g., GPT-5.4) catches a different class of issues because different models have different blind spots.

Today I have to either duplicate the QA agent file with a hardcoded model, or pause the workflow and ask the user to switch models in the picker. With a `model` parameter on `runSubagent`, the orchestrator could do this automatically:

```
// Pseudocode of desired behavior
runSubagent({ agentName: "qa-investigator", prompt: "...", model: "Claude Opus 4" })
// ... iterate until clean ...
runSubagent({ agentName: "qa-investigator", prompt: "...", model: "GPT-5.4" })
// ... iterate until clean ...
```

### Proposed Solution

Add an optional `model` parameter to the `runSubagent` tool that overrides the subagent's frontmatter `model` (or the inherited picker model) for that single invocation:

```typescript
runSubagent({
agentName: string,
prompt: string,
description: string,
model?: string // Optional: override the subagent's model for this invocation
})
```

Semantics:
- If `model` is provided, use it for this invocation regardless of the subagent's frontmatter or the user's picker selection
- If `model` is omitted, current behavior is preserved (subagent uses its frontmatter model, or inherits the picker model)
- The model override applies only to the subagent invocation, not to the parent agent

### Alternative Solutions

- **Workspace setting mapping agent names to models** — less flexible, can't change per-invocation
- **A `model-override` frontmatter field** — static, doesn't solve the "same agent, different models at different stages" problem
- **Duplicating agent files with different models** — current workaround, works but creates maintenance burden

### Prior Art

- [#281978](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/281978) requested per-agent `model:` in frontmatter (now supported). This request goes one step further: per-*invocation* model override.
- **GitHub Copilot CLI** already supports specifying a model when invoking subagents, allowing orchestrator agents to route different workflow stages to different models without duplicating agent definitions or requiring user intervention.
- **Claude Code CLI's** `Task` tool similarly supports `model:` as an invocation parameter for subagents.
- The `chat.exploreAgent.defaultModel` setting ([#297184](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297184)) shows per-agent model routing is already implemented internally for built-in agents.

The capability exists in both the Copilot CLI and Claude Code CLI — this request is about bringing the same per-invocation model override to the VS Code Copilot Chat extension's `runSubagent` tool.

### Environment
- VS Code Insiders 2026-04-02
- GitHub Copilot Chat 0.43.x
- OS: macOS

audit_exclusions.query_title: Node not saving coverage when process is terminated using SIGINT/SIGTERM
audit_exclusions.query_body:
* **Version**: v14.10.1

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

When running this code
```
function run() {
if (1) {
console.log(1);
} else {
console.log(2);
}
}

run();

setTimeout(process.exit, 3000)
```

If I stop the process using SIGINT/SIGTERM before the timeout kicks in, coverage is not saved.

```
% NODE_V8_COVERAGE=/tmp/cov node /tmp/t.js
1
^C
% ls /tmp/cov
ls: cannot access '/tmp/cov': No such file or directory
%

```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node coverage should work in the same way as other coverage tools, saving the coverage before terminating the process even if no SIGINT handler is set.

### What do you see instead?

No coverage is saved.

### Additional information

I know that adding a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler can be used as a workaround but this is not how most applications terminate and has no added value.
```
process.on('SIGINT', () => process.exit())
process.on('SIGTERM', () => process.exit())
```

audit_exclusions.query_title: Node.js dns.getServers() returns 127.0.0.1 on Windows 11 while Windows DNS is configured correctly, causing dns.resolveSrv() and MongoDB Atlas (mongodb+srv://) to fail
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### Version

v24.18.0 , v22.22.0 Issue reproduced on both versions.

### Platform

```text
Windows 11 24H2 (Build 10.0.26200) x64
```

### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

1. Install Node.js (tested with v22.22.0 and v24.18.0) on Windows 11 (Build 10.0.26200).

2. Save the following as `repro.js`:

```js
const dns = require("node:dns");

console.log("Node:", process.version);
console.log("Servers:", dns.getServers());

dns.lookup("google.com", (err, address) => {
console.log("lookup:", err, address);
});

dns.resolve4("google.com", (err, addresses) => {
console.log("resolve4:", err, addresses);
});

dns.resolveSrv("_mongodb._tcp.cluster0.mongodb.net", (err, records) => {
console.log("resolveSrv:", err, records);
});
```

3. Run:

```bash
node repro.js
```

4. Observe the output.

### Output

```
Node: v22.22.0
Servers: [ '127.0.0.1' ]

resolve4:
Error: queryA ECONNREFUSED google.com

resolveSrv:
Error: querySrv ECONNREFUSED _mongodb._tcp.cluster0.mongodb.net

lookup:
null 2404:6800:4013:804::64
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

The issue reproduces 100% of the time on my machine.

Conditions:
- Windows 11 (Build 10.0.26200)
- Reproduced with Node.js v22.22.0 and v24.18.0
- Occurs regardless of whether I am connected via Wi-Fi or a mobile hotspot.
- No proxy is configured.
- Windows DNS resolution works correctly (`nslookup` and `Resolve-DnsName` both succeed).
- `dns.getServers()` consistently returns `['127.0.0.1']`.
- `dns.lookup()` succeeds.
- `dns.resolve4()` and `dns.resolveSrv()` fail with `ECONNREFUSED`.
- Calling `dns.setServers(["8.8.8.8", "1.1.1.1"])` before performing DNS resolution makes the issue disappear.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`dns.getServers()` should return the DNS servers configured by the operating system rather than `127.0.0.1`, since Windows is configured to use DHCP-assigned DNS servers.

On my system:

- `ipconfig /all` reports:
- IPv4 DNS: `10.219.174.109`
- IPv6 DNS: `2409:40c2:8427:7b61::c7`

- `nslookup` works correctly.
- `Resolve-DnsName` works correctly.
- `dns.lookup()` works correctly.

Therefore I expect:

- `dns.getServers()` to report the DNS servers configured by Windows.
- `dns.resolve4()` and `dns.resolveSrv()` to successfully resolve DNS records without requiring an explicit call to `dns.setServers()`.

Instead, `dns.getServers()` reports `['127.0.0.1']`, causing `dns.resolve4()` and `dns.resolveSrv()` to fail with `ECONNREFUSED`.

### What do you see instead?

Instead of using the DNS servers configured by Windows, `dns.getServers()` returns:

```text
[ '127.0.0.1' ]
```

As a result:

- `dns.lookup()` succeeds because it uses the operating system's resolver.
- `dns.resolve4()` fails with `ECONNREFUSED`.
- `dns.resolveSrv()` fails with `ECONNREFUSED`.

Output:

```text
Node: v22.22.0

Servers:
[ '127.0.0.1' ]

resolve4:
Error: queryA ECONNREFUSED google.com
code: 'ECONNREFUSED'
syscall: 'queryA'

resolveSrv:
Error: querySrv ECONNREFUSED _mongodb._tcp.cluster0.mongodb.net
code: 'ECONNREFUSED'
syscall: 'querySrv'

lookup:
null 2404:6800:4013:804::64
```

Additionally, calling:

```js
const dns = require("node:dns");
dns.setServers(["8.8.8.8", "1.1.1.1"]);
```

before the DNS queries immediately resolves the issue:

- `dns.resolve4()` succeeds.
- `dns.resolveSrv()` succeeds.
- MongoDB Atlas connections using `mongodb+srv://` work correctly.

### Additional information

The issue disappears if I explicitly configure DNS servers before performing DNS resolution:

```js
const dns = require("node:dns");

dns.setServers(["8.8.8.8", "1.1.1.1"]);
```

After calling `dns.setServers()`:

- `dns.resolve4()` succeeds.
- `dns.resolveSrv()` succeeds.
- MongoDB Atlas connections using `mongodb+srv://` work normally.

This suggests that the failure is related to the default DNS server configuration returned by `dns.getServers()`, which reports `127.0.0.1` on my system.
audit_exclusions.target_title: dns.getServers() incorrectly returns 127.0.0.1 when OS DNS is configured to 8.8.8.8

audit_exclusions.query_body:
### Version

v22.10.0

### Platform

```text
Darwin Silmaril.home 23.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 23.6.0: Wed Jul 31 20:49:46 PDT 2024; root:xnu-10063.141.1.700.5~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T8103 arm64
```

### Subsystem

vm

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

```js
const vm = require('node:vm');

const context = vm.createContext({ structuredClone });
const result = vm.runInContext('structuredClone(new Error()) instanceof Error', context);

console.log('match:', result);
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

100%

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`match: true` because `structuredClone` should use the context of the VM for the prototype of the produced `Error` instance.

### What do you see instead?

```match: false```

Additional investigation shows that the produced `Error` uses the prototype of the main runtime. Ie. a context escape, which would be a security error, if not for the disclaimer not to run untrusted code.

### Additional information

This issue also applies to all other cloneable types like `Map`. Even `Object` fails `instanceof`:

```js
structuredClone({}) instanceof Object // <= equals false inside VM
```

FYI, this causes problems when running tests in jest, which use the VM to run tests.

audit_exclusions.query_title: Expose JSON Schema validation as a public API
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

PR #62603 is vendoring `ata-validator` into Node.js core for `node.config.json` validation. During that review, @TheOneTheOnlyJJ and @h4ad both asked whether ata could be exposed to user code once it's vendored in.

Every project that needs JSON Schema validation today pulls in a third-party dependency. If Node is already shipping a validator internally, it feels odd not to let user code reach it.

Opening this to check if the direction is something the project wants to pursue, and to collect thoughts on naming and scope before anyone writes a prototype PR.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Expose ata as a built-in `node:` module, using the same runtime that #62603 is vendoring.

Three names came up in discussion:

- `node:schema`, focused on JSON Schema
- `node:jsonschema`, more specific
- `node:json`, wider, covering parse and validate together (ata already vendors simdjson)

Rough sketch:

```js
import { Validator } from 'node:schema'

const v = new Validator({
type: 'object',
properties: { id: { type: 'integer' } },
required: ['id'],
})

v.validate({ id: 1 }) // { valid: true, errors: [] }
```

Would probably land this behind an experimental flag first, the way `node:test` started. Happy to put together a prototype PR if the direction is one the project wants to pursue.

### What alternatives have you considered?

1. Keep the vendor scoped to `node.config.json` only (current #62603 plan). Downside: Node ships a validator user code can't reach.

2. Schema-only module (`node:schema` / `node:jsonschema`). Narrow scope, leaves simdjson for another issue.

3. Combined `node:json` module. Covers parse and validate together, bigger API surface.

4. Third-party package that depends on Node internals. Ruled out, defeats the point of vendoring.

No strong preference between 2 and 3. Would rather hear from the Node collaborators and folks who already commented on #62603 before picking.
audit_exclusions.target_title: JSON Schema validation in Node.js core

4. Switch your input method to Japanese IME (Input Method Editor).

audit_exclusions.query_title: Embedding: Distribute official libnode.so/dll/dylib bins
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

Currently Node is distributed officially as an executable binary here: [https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.15.0/](https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.15.0/).

For applications that intend to embed libnode, embedders must manually compile and distribute libnode.

There are projects like [https://github.com/metacall/libnode](https://github.com/metacall/libnode) that distribute prebuilt copies of libnode however it would be amazing if there was a reliable official source to fetch libnode as it would help with distributing applications that depend on it.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Distribute prebuilt libnode binaries from the Nodejs website. For example:
```
https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.15.0/libnode-v22.15.0-linux-x64.tar.xz
```

With a reliable url to fetch libnode, embedders could package/distribute libnode along with their applications or fetch libnode dynamically on the first run of their application.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Compiling libnode myself or using unofficial prebuilt packages

audit_exclusions.query_title: Explicit glob argument for test runner?
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

Unless I'm missing something, it seems that at the moment the glob arguments are only recognized when they are the last arguments. So the common `npm run test -- --test-only` or `npm run test -- --test-update-snapshots` pattern doesn't work. This results in having to copy/paste the glob arguments in all the test scripts. Here's what it looks like in a project of mine that uses typescript:

```json
{
"scripts": {
"test": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --test '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts'",
"test:only": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --test-only --test '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts'",
"test:watch": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --watch --watch-path-ignore=generated/ --test '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts'",
"test:update": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --test --test-update-snapshots '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts'",
"test:coverage": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-coverage-exclude='**/generated/**' --test-coverage-exclude='node_modules/**' --test-coverage-functions=80 --experimental-test-coverage '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts'",
"test:coverage:lcov": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --test --test-reporter=lcov --test-coverage-exclude='**/generated/**' --test-coverage-exclude='node_modules/**' --test-coverage-functions=80 --experimental-test-coverage '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts' > coverage/lcov.info",
}
}
```

This is obviously prone to error.

I tried a few different ways to avoid repeating the globs all over the place but nothing seemed to work (well, there's always the option of writing scripts outside `package.json` but it would be nice if it wasn't necessary).

If the globs were named, e.g. `--glob='**/*.test.ts' --glob='**/test/**/*.ts'` or if it was allowed to put more arguments after them e.g. `--test '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts' --test-only`, it would then be possible to rewrite the above as:

```json
{
"scripts": {
"test": "NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --test '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts'",
"test:only": "npm test -- --test-only",
"test:watch": "npm test -- --watch --watch-path-ignore=generated/",
"test:update": "npm test -- --test-update-snapshots",
"test:coverage": "npm test -- --test-reporter=spec --test-coverage-exclude='**/generated/**' --test-coverage-exclude='node_modules/**' --test-coverage-functions=80 --experimental-test-coverage",
"test:coverage:lcov": "npm test -- --test-reporter=lcov --test-coverage-exclude='**/generated/**' --test-coverage-exclude='node_modules/**' --test-coverage-functions=80 --experimental-test-coverage > coverage/lcov.info",
}
}

```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

See above.

### What alternatives have you considered?

1) Named arguments , e.g.:

`--test-include='**/*.test.ts' --test-include='/test/**/*.ts'`

2) Simply treating the globs as arguments to `--test` and keep parsing other arguments after.

e.g.: `--test '**/*.test.ts' '**/test/**/*.ts' --test-only --other-arg --etc`

3) Configuration in package.json instead of CLI argument:

```json
{

"test": {
"include": ["**/*.test.ts", "/test/**/*.ts"]
}
}
```

S

audit_exclusions.query_title: Native support of TSX
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

It will simplify a lot the life of novices to web-dev ecosystem to have simpler support for running server-side rendering using TSX

My usecase: simple server-side rendering of Lexical JSON's https://github.com/vadimkantorov/lexical-cli-render from CLI. Currently I had to use ts-node, because Node did not support importing custom controls defined in TSX.

Discussed it in https://github.com/orgs/nodejs/discussions/57070

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

It appears that SWC (used by Amaro under the hood) already has support for TSX: https://swc.rs/blog/swc-1#typescript-support

But it seems disabled by Node: https://nodejs.org/api/typescript.html#determining-module-system

I assume that deciding on TSX support should also correlate somehow with decisions on JSX:
- https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/56822

In this linked issue the main blocker seems to be design of running various code transformations. I hope it does not block the feature, as even streamlining some basic usecases would be of great help to novices.

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_

audit_exclusions.query_title: Add a npm: prefix to import for compatibility between the browser and Node
audit_exclusions.query_body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

Now that modules are supported in the browser, I can import "./node_modules," but that is awkward and does not have the same semantics as a node import.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Now that modules are well-supported, I can use them in the browser, but I need to specify "./node_modules" on import. However, it isn't fully compatible with Node. An **npm:** prefix could be ignored by Node but interpreted by servers. It would be even better if there were a library for applying standard Node module rules for use with Express and other server platforms.

### What alternatives have you considered?

I use import .. "./node_modules" and try to avoid pitfalls. However, it is far from transparent since changes in the modules aren't hidden.

audit_exclusions.query_title: Utility method for exposing Node’s type resolution
audit_exclusions.query_body:
Split off from https://github.com/nodejs/modules/issues/389#issuecomment-537228049. I think it would be useful to have a function that returns how Node would try to interpret a file, in particular whether Node would try to parse a path to a `.js` file as CommonJS or as ESM. This would spare tools from needing to reimplement Node’s “find the nearest parent `package.json` and see if it has a `"type"` field” algorithm.

Whether the file would be interpreted successfully as that type is irrelevant; it could be a zero-byte file for all this API cares. One use case for this is for tools loading `.js` config files to know whether to try to load the files via `require` or `import()`.

```Rust
fn main() {
match return { return } {}
}
```

| ^^ ^^
|
= note: `#[warn(unused_braces)]` (part of `#[warn(unused)]`) on by default
help: remove these braces
|
2 - match return { return } {}
2 + match return return {}
|

warning: unreachable expression
--> src/main.rs:2:11
|
2 | match return { return } {}
| ^^^^^^^^^------^^
| | |
| | any code following this expression is unreachable
| unreachable expression
|
= note: `#[warn(unreachable_code)]` (part of `#[warn(unused)]`) on by default

Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.60s

`unused_braces` should not be fired, as the suggested code

```rust
fn main() {
match return return {}
}
```

doesn’t compile:

3 | }

error: could not compile `playground` (bin "playground") due to 1 previous error

_No response_

Formatted code

```rust

return

}

audit_exclusions.query_title: `cargo install rust-update` fails, because linker not found.
audit_exclusions.query_body:
After successfully installing rust from `rust-1.97.1-x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm.msi` with `msiexec /I rust-1.97.1-x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm.msi TARGETDIR=C:\prgs\rust INSTALLDIR=C:\prgs\rust INSTALLFOLDER=C:\prgs\rust ALLUSERS="" /l*v log.txt`. rust was installed without mingw, because `msys` is in path. I tried this code: ```rust cargo install rust-update ``` I expected to see this happen: to install `rust-update` without hasles. Instead, this happened: ``` > cargo install rust-update Updating crates.io index Installing rust-update v0.1.0 Updating crates.io index Compiling rust-update v0.1.0 error: linker `x86_64-w64-mingw32-clang` not found | = note: program not found error: could not compile `rust-update` (bin "rust-update") due to 1 previous error error: failed to compile `rust-update v0.1.0`, intermediate artifacts can be found at `C:\Users\scth-muc\AppData\Local\Temp\cargo-install9QcQj7`. To reuse those artifacts with a future compilation, set the environment variable `CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR` to that path. ``` Seems rust installs in a way not usable afterwards if msys, cygwin or mingw is installed sowwhere else. ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14) binary: rustc commit-hash: 8bab26f4f68e0e26f0bb7960be334d5b520ea452 commit-date: 2026-07-14 host: x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm release: 1.97.1 LLVM version: 22.1.6 ```

audit_exclusions.query_title: ICE: Found unstable fingerprints for explicit_supertraits_containing_assoc_item on incremental rebuild when any #[derive] is added
audit_exclusions.query_body:
I tried to get the MRE but after a whole afternoon failed to do so, and try to throw claude on to this work of getting the MRE but opus still fails. what we find is basically (these text, some are copied from claude but others are edited/written by myself):
## Summary

Running `cargo +nightly check` (or `cargo +nightly clippy`) on the
[bincode v3-release branch](https://github.com/bincode-org/bincode/tree/v3-release)
produces an ICE on the second incremental build after any `#[derive(...)]`
is added to the crate.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Apich-Organization/bincode
cd bincode
git checkout v3-release

# Step 1 — prime the incremental cache
cargo +nightly check --features alloc,std,derive,serde

# Step 2 — any edit that adds a #[derive]; a plain comment is NOT enough
# #[derive(Copy, Clone)]
# struct _Trigger;
printf '\n#[derive(Copy, Clone)] struct _Trigger;\n' >> src/lib.rs

# Step 3 — ICE on the second incremental build
cargo +nightly check --features alloc,std,derive,serde
```

**ICE output**
```text
error: internal compiler error: encountered incremental compilation error with
explicit_supertraits_containing_assoc_item(39269fc2b6d68024-cd3d7d3d559ab5ba)

Found unstable fingerprints for
explicit_supertraits_containing_assoc_item(39269fc2b6d68024-cd3d7d3d559ab5ba):
EarlyBinder { value: [(
Binder { value: TraitPredicate(<Self as core::marker::MetaSized>, polarity:Positive),
bound_vars: [] },
src/config.rs:719:5: 721:6 (#2978)
)], .. }

query stack during panic:
#0 [explicit_supertraits_containing_assoc_item] computing the super traits of
`config::internal::InternalEndianConfig` with associated type name `Mode`
#1 [typeck_root] type-checking `features::impl_alloc::encode_to_vec`
```

[rustc-ice-2026-06-19T12_59_41-8484.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29137707/rustc-ice-2026-06-19T12_59_41-8484.txt)

**Workaround**

```bash
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo +nightly check --features alloc,std,derive,serde
```

**Toolchain**

```text
rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c1b22f44c 2026-06-17)
```
Both on x86_64 linux and windows.

**Related issues**

There is a very similar issue under rust-clippy, [rust-lang/rust-clippy#17262](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy/issues/17262) but I found it to not only a issue with clippy, so I opened the issue here again.

**Notes**
* cargo +nightly clippy and cargo +nightly check both trigger the ICE
* CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 is the workaround
* A truly minimal self-contained reproduction has not been found yet; it appears
the ICE requires the project to have many existing proc-macro expansions (from
bincode-derive) before the relevant query fires, so that the synthesized
MetaSized SyntaxContext is large enough to shift detectably. Contributions to
further minimization are welcome.

Also here's some analysis coauthored by me and LLM, but, well, myself is not a active member in the rustc project so this could be only for reference:

---

The explicit_supertraits_containing_assoc_item query for InternalEndianConfig
returns a MetaSized supertrait predicate. MetaSized is synthesized by the
nightly compiler (from the sized_hierarchy feature) with a freshly-allocated
SyntaxContext ID. The ID's value depends on how many macro expansions have
occurred in the current session before the synthesis point.

Between sessions, the number of prior expansions changes when any #[derive(...)]
is added: the new derive proc-macro expansion shifts the SyntaxContext counter by k
before InternalEndianConfig's supertraits are computed. So the cached fingerprint
(SyntaxContext N) differs from the recomputed one (SyntaxContext N+k) → ICE.

Notably, plain comments do NOT reproduce the bug — only items with #[derive]
(or other macro-expanding annotations) do, because only those advance the
SyntaxContext counter.

*Relevant trait structure*
The essential traits involved (from src/config.rs):

```rust
// Trait with NO explicit supertraits — MetaSized is its only implicit supertrait.
// The MetaSized supertrait predicate gets a session-dependent SyntaxContext → ICE.
pub(crate) trait InternalEndianConfig {
const ENDIAN: Endianness;
}

// Trait that carries the associated type `Mode`
pub(crate) trait InternalFingerprintConfigExt {
type Mode;
}

// Combined trait
pub(crate) trait Config:
InternalEndianConfig + ... + InternalFingerprintConfigExt + Copy + Clone { ... }
```
And the trigger function in src/lib.rs (via features/):

```rust
pub fn encode_to_vec<E: Encode, C: Config>(val: E, config: C) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EncodeError>
where
C::Mode: InternalFingerprintGuard<E, C>,
```
Resolving C::Mode walks all supertraits of Config — including InternalEndianConfig
— calling explicit_supertraits_containing_assoc_item(InternalEndianConfig, "Mode").
That result (the MetaSized predicate with non-deterministic SyntaxContext) gets cached
in session 1, then mismatches in session 2 when the SyntaxContext counter shifts.

---

And anyway, I am working on try to find the MRE, but well, a little bit hard...

audit_exclusions.query_title: implied bound related unsoundness
audit_exclusions.query_body:
This is almost identical to the [unsound example test case](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/4f84d9fac456d973d592cf3fb48db958ecf22506/tests/ui/implied-bounds/implied-bounds-on-nested-references-plus-variance-2.rs) for issue-25860. The difference is that this variant only began compiling successfully since `nightly-2020-06-24`, whereas the existing known unsoundness already compiles since nightly-2015-02-18 (rustc 1.0.0). I tried this code: ```rust static UNIT: &'static &'static () = &&(); fn foo<'a, 'b, T>(_: &'a &'b (), v: &'b T) -> &'a T { v } fn bad<'a, T>(x: &'a T) -> &'static T { let f: fn(_, &T) -> &'static T = foo; f(UNIT, x) } fn main() { let r: &'static String; { let s = String::from("temporary"); r = bad(&s); println!("while alive: {}", r); } println!("use-after-free reads: {}", r); } ``` The only difference from that test case is the number of parameters and arguments in `foo`. audit_exclusions.query_body:
### Code

minimal proc-macro import `src/lib.rs`:
```Rust
extern crate my_macro;

pub use thiserror_impl::*;
```

minimal proc-macro:
```Rust
`impl/src/lib.rs`:

extern crate proc_macro;

use proc_macro::TokenStream;

#[proc_macro_derive(Error, attributes(backtrace, error, from, source))]
pub fn derive_error(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
loop {}
}
```

to run:
```bash
rustc +nightly --edition=2024 --crate-type=proc-macro -Zsanitizer=address --crate-name=my_macro impl/src/lib.rs
rustc +nightly --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name=my_lib --extern=my_macro=libmy_macro.so src/lib2.rs
```

I tried this code:

```rust
macro_rules! a {
($a:path) => {
const _: () = $a!();
};
}

a! {std::println}
```

I expected to see this happen: An error that `println!()` is not allowed in const contexts.

Instead, this happened: ``expected one of `.`, `;`, `?`, `where`, or an operator, found `!` ``

However the following does correctly parse:

```rust
macro_rules! a {
($a:path) => {
const _: () = {
$a!();
};
};
}

a! {std::println}
```

### Code ```Rust #![feature(dispatch_from_dyn, unsize, arbitrary_self_types)] use std::marker::Unsize; use std::ops::{DispatchFromDyn, Receiver}; #[repr(align(65536))] pub struct Ptr<'a, T: ?Sized>(&'a T); impl<'a, T: ?Sized, U: ?Sized> DispatchFromDyn> for Ptr<'a, T> where T: Unsize {} impl<'a, T: ?Sized> Receiver for Ptr<'a, T> { type Target = T; } pub trait Trait { fn method(self: Ptr<'_, Self>); } pub fn call(ptr: Ptr) { ptr.method(); } ``` Requires `cargo build` to reproduce the ICE. `cargo check` does not cause the ICE. `DispatchFromDyn` probably has to also prohibit `repr(align)`, like how it currently prohibits `repr(packed)` or `repr(C)`. cc @dingxiangfei2009 ### Meta Reproducible on the playground with version `1.96.0-nightly (2026-04-05 9602bda1dd0c1bbf5787)` ### Error output ``` error: internal compiler error: /rustc-dev/9602bda1dd0c1bbf5787e398385bbac81fd532f8/compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/abi.rs:756:18: receiver type has unsupported layout: TyAndLayout { ty: Ptr<'_, dyn Trait>, layout: Layout { size: Size(65536 bytes), align: AbiAlign { abi: Align(65536 bytes) }, backend_repr: Memory { sized: true }, fields: Arbitrary { offsets: [Size(0 bytes)], in_memory_order: [0] }, largest_niche: Some(Niche { offset: Size(0 bytes), value: Pointer(AddressSpace(0)), valid_range: 1..=18446744073709551615 }), uninhabited: false, variants: Single { index: 0 }, max_repr_align: Some(Align(65536 bytes)), unadjusted_abi_align: Align(8 bytes), randomization_seed: 1452713011452813251 } } thread 'rustc' (41) panicked at /rustc-dev/9602bda1dd0c1bbf5787e398385bbac81fd532f8/compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/abi.rs:756:18: Box ```

audit_exclusions.query_body:
### Code ```Rust #![feature(adt_const_params, unsized_const_params, generic_const_parameter_types)] #![allow(incomplete_features)] trait Object<'a, const N: &'a u32> {} fn binder(param: &dyn for<'a> Object<'a, true>) {} fn main() {} ``` Discovered in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/152931 Three stages of what "should" happen: - Currently it should probably `//@ check-pass`, ignoring the type error, instead of ICEing. - Next, `feature(generic_const_parameter_types)` should probably disallow ConstArgHasType obligations to reference lifetimes introduced by a sibling in the binder that introduces the const parameter (i.e. ban `for<'a, const N: &'a u32>`). - Eventually, in a possible cool future world, generic_const_parameter_types will allow that, and it should type error on the fact that `true` is not a `&'a u32`. ### Meta tested on my rustc checkout https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/d8b2222b11fc03a31d43707c8c9006f025809ece and also ices on stable: `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.93.1 (01f6ddf75 2026-02-11) binary: rustc commit-hash: 01f6ddf7588f42ae2d7eb0a2f21d44e8e96674cf commit-date: 2026-02-11 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.93.1 LLVM version: 21.1.8 ``` ### Error output

audit_exclusions.query_title: Deriving Default for non-default generics should work in trivial cases
audit_exclusions.query_body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

```rust
struct NoDefault {}

#[derive(Default)]
struct VecHolder<T> {
data: Vec<T>,
}

fn main() {
let x: VecHolder<NoDefault> = VecHolder::default();
}
```

This produces an error:
```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `NoDefault: Default` is not satisfied
--> <source>:9:35
|
9 | let x: VecHolder<NoDefault> = VecHolder::default();
| ^^^^^^^^^ the trait `Default` is not implemented for `NoDefault`
|
help: the trait `Default` is implemented for `VecHolder<T>`
--> <source>:3:10
|
3 | #[derive(Default)]
| ^^^^^^^
note: required for `VecHolder<NoDefault>` to implement `Default`
--> <source>:3:10
|
3 | #[derive(Default)]
| ^^^^^^^ unsatisfied trait bound introduced in this `derive` macro
help: consider annotating `NoDefault` with `#[derive(Default)]`
|
1 + #[derive(Default)]
2 | struct NoDefault {}
|
```

I expected this to compile, because `Default` implementation for `Vec<T>` does not require `T: Default`
Moreover, you can define it trivially yourself:
```rust
struct NoDefault {}

struct VecHolder<T> {
data: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T> Default for VecHolder<T> {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
data: Default::default()
}
}
}

fn main() {
let x: VecHolder<NoDefault> = VecHolder::default();
}
```
...and this works.

`rustc --version --verbose`:
I'm using Godbolt compiler 1.93.0 (https://godbolt.org/z/GMd1nvMjz), but it's the same with pretty much any other major version, including current nightly
