audit_exclusions.query_title: Partial architecture mismatch: X86_64 objects found in precompiled libcompiler_builtins for loongarch64-unknown-none
audit_exclusions.query_body: I am cross-compiling a kernel project from an **x86_64 Linux host** to the **loongarch64-unknown-none** target using a Makefile. ```bash cargo build --release --target loongarch64-unknown-none --no-default-features --features "board_la2k1000" ``` I expected to see this happen: *Successful linkage for LoongArch64 target.* Instead, this happened: *rust-lld: error: /home/pillow/.rustup/toolchains/nightly-2024-02-03-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/loongarch64-unknown-none/lib/libcompiler_builtins-781bb25c3f16ec1d.rlib(45c91108d938afe8-absvdi2.o) is incompatible with /tmp/rustcE4rpQv/symbols.o* ### deep analysis I extracted the objects from the precompiled `libcompiler_builtins` rlib and found a partial architecture mismatch. While Rust-generated objects are correct (LoongArch), the C-based objects from `compiler-rt` are incorrectly compiled for **X86_64**. Evidence from `llvm-readelf -h`(because many of the files are x86_64, i just show one of them): ```bash File: ./libcompiler_builtins-781bb25c3f16ec1d.rlib(45c91108d938afe8-ucmpti2.o) ELF Header: Magic: 7f 45 4c 46 02 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 Class: ELF64 Data: 2's complement, little endian Version: 1 (current) OS/ABI: UNIX - System V ABI Version: 0 Type: REL (Relocatable file) Machine: Advanced Micro Devices X86-64 Version: 0x1 Entry point address: 0x0 Start of program headers: 0 (bytes into file) Start of section headers: 3008 (bytes into file) Flags: 0x0 Size of this header: 64 (bytes) Size of program headers: 0 (bytes) Number of program headers: 0 Size of section headers: 64 (bytes) Number of section headers: 23 Section header string table index: 22 ``` ### Verification from Official Source To rule out any local environment issues or `rustup` corruption, I manually downloaded the original component directly from the official distribution server: `https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/2024-02-03/rust-std-nightly-loongarch64-unknown-none.tar.xz` After extracting this fresh download, the results were identical: the C-based objects (e.g., `absvdi2.o`) are still `X86_64`. This confirms the issue originates from the upstream distribution itself. Evidence from "llvm-readelf": ```bash ~/Dow/t/r/r/lib/rustlib/loongarch64-unknown-none/lib ❯ llvm-readelf -h ./45c91108d938afe8-absvdi2.o  10:37:37 PM ELF Header: Magic: 7f 45 4c 46 02 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 Class: ELF64 Data: 2's complement, little endian Version: 1 (current) OS/ABI: UNIX - System V ABI Version: 0 Type: REL (Relocatable file) Machine: Advanced Micro Devices X86-64 Version: 0x1 Entry point address: 0x0 Start of program headers: 0 (bytes into file) Start of section headers: 4144 (bytes into file) Flags: 0x0 Size of this header: 64 (bytes) Size of program headers: 0 (bytes) Number of program headers: 0 Size of section headers: 64 (bytes) Number of section headers: 28 Section header string table index: 27 ``` ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.77.0-nightly (bf3c6c5be 2024-02-01) binary: rustc commit-hash: bf3c6c5bed498f41ad815641319a1ad9bcecb8e8 commit-date: 2024-02-01 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.77.0-nightly LLVM version: 17.0.6 ```

audit_exclusions.query_title: ICE: `expected specialization failed to hold` when using specialization with RPITIT and unresolved type in `where` clause
audit_exclusions.query_body:
I found an ICE when fuzzing `specialization` combined with RPITIT (`-> impl Sized`). It seems that when a `where` clause in a specializing impl refers to an unresolved type (name resolution failure), the compiler fails to recover gracefully and asserts during generic parameter translation in the specialization graph verification. I tried this code: ```rust #![feature(specialization)] trait Base { fn call(&self) -> impl Sized; } default impl Base for T where T: Copy, { fn call(&self) -> T { *self } } #[derive(Copy, Clone)] struct Item; impl Base for Item where T: Base, {} fn main() { Item.call(); } ``` I expected to see this happen: The compiler should emit `error[E0425]: cannot find type T in this scope` and exit gracefully (or continue analysis without crashing). Instead, this happened: The compiler panicked with an internal compiler error. ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.94.0-nightly (e29fcf45e 2026-01-04) binary: rustc commit-hash: e29fcf45e4ae686d77b490bf07320f0d3a2cf35f commit-date: 2026-01-04 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.94.0-nightly LLVM version: 21.1.8 ```

### Code [playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=e33362c7b4731f262abf2d47e1e2a460) ```Rust trait UnderlyingImpl { type InfoType: LevelInfo; type SupportedArray; } trait LevelInfo { const SUPPORTED_SLOTS: usize; } struct Info; impl LevelInfo for Info { const SUPPORTED_SLOTS: usize = 1; } struct SomeImpl; impl UnderlyingImpl for SomeImpl { type InfoType = Info; // This line makes compiler panic type SupportedArray = [T; ::SUPPORTED_SLOTS]; // But this works //type SupportedArray = [T; ::SUPPORTED_SLOTS]; } ``` ### Meta (local) `rustc --version --verbose`: Same behavior on [playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=e33362c7b4731f262abf2d47e1e2a460) (both stable and nightly) ``` rustc 1.90.0-nightly (8f08b3a32 2025-07-18) binary: rustc commit-hash: 8f08b3a32478b8d0507732800ecb548a76e0fd0c commit-date: 2025-07-18 host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc release: 1.90.0-nightly LLVM version: 20.1.8 ```

audit_exclusions.query_title: [Low] unsafe_block: Unnecessary unsafe block in unwind/src/unwinding.rs (line 74)
audit_exclusions.query_body:
[[ I tried this code: ```rust // 代码来源:rust/library/unwind/src/unwinding.rs (line 74) // 缺陷:使用不必要的unsafe块进行指针转换,可通过安全方式实现 let ctx = unsafe { &mut *(ctx as *mut UnwindContext<'_>) }; ``` I expected to see this happen: * * 移除不必要的unsafe代码块,通过Rust的安全类型转换或API实现相同逻辑(例如:若`ctx`的类型本身支持安全的可变引用转换,直接使用类型系统约束的安全操作); * 避免无必要的unsafe使用,降低代码的安全风险与攻击面。* Instead, this happened: * * 缺陷类型:不必要的unsafe代码块(Low风险,对应比赛评价权重1); * 实际行为:使用unsafe块进行可通过安全方式完成的指针转换,增加了代码的安全风险与攻击面; * 影响:不必要的unsafe会降低代码的可维护性,且可能掩盖潜在的类型安全问题,违背Rust“最小化unsafe范围”的编码规范。* ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.94.0-nightly (e7d44143a 2025-12-24)binary: rustccommit-hash: e7d44143a12a526488e4f0c0d7ea8e62a4fe9354commit-date: 2025-12-24host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvcrelease: 1.94.0-nightlyLLVM version: 21.1.8 ```
Backtrace

```

Note (No runtime backtrace for this issue)

This issue is a code规范 defect (unnecessary unsafe block) rather than a runtime error, so no backtrace is generated. The risk lies in avoidable unsafe usage that increases code complexity and potential vulnerabilities.
```
